thread:
alex: Heads up — found a service account key accidentally included in a package.json published to the public GitHub Package Registry. Not the container image, the metadata file. Saw it via repo-scanner. Path: packages/payments/package.json
sara: can you paste the exact key id (no secret) and which SA?
alex: Key id prefix: 0A3F4... IAM: service-account-llm-deploy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com. I'll DM the full key to mika_sec.
mika_sec: moving this to incident. Creating containment plan. @deploy-bot please create an incident.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created by mika_sec. Severity: P2. Tags: secrets, kms, rotation.
mike_ops: Immediate steps: 1) disable key 2) revoke tokens 3) rotate any KMS-wrapped items. Who can run KMS rewrap?
jess_dev: quick check: did CI publish this with PACKAGES_TOKEN? Running `grep -R "service-account-llm-deploy" .github/workflows || true` in the repo.
alex: pipeline didn't use it; looks like an old deploy SA that was embedded in package metadata at publish time. Not used in runtime.
sara: still need rotation and audit. Enable export of admin and data access logs for iam.serviceAccounts.keys and Cloud KMS for the last 30 days.
mika_sec: I'll disable the key now. @sam_oncall can you run the revoke command? Command: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable 0A3F4... --iam-account=service-account-llm-deploy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
sam_oncall: running now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable 0A3F4... --iam-account=service-account-llm-deploy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
deploy-bot: Deployment freeze enabled for affected repos: packages/payments, infra/publishers. Reason: secret leak.
mike_ops: Next: rotate any Vault entries referencing that SA. We need a search across Vault for the SA email. Jess, can you run a scoped lookup rather than global creds?
jess_dev: I'll run lookup using an ephemeral least-priv token: `vault kv list -format=json secret | xargs -I{} vault kv get -format=json secret/{}` — coordinating with mika_sec for token creation.
mika_sec: don't use wide tokens in the channel. Creating an ephemeral token: `vault token create -period=1h -policy=security-search` and DMing it to jess_dev.
alex: Also plan for KMS rewrap: if any ciphertexts were encrypted with this SA's keys, we'll create a new key version and re-encrypt. Example: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...` then re-encrypt artifacts.
sam_oncall: audit logs snapshot uploaded to gs://secops-incident/INC-2026-045/. Included: admin activity, data access, KMS logs. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/secops-incident/INC-2026-045/
sara: containment checklist (short): - disable leaked key - create replacement SA with minimal perms - rotate Vault entries - rewrap KMS ciphertexts - revoke OAuth tokens and CI creds - run package registry scan and notify partners if needed
mika_sec: RBAC follow-up: remove iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin from broad groups, enforce impersonation via iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy + short-lived tokens. Scheduling RBAC audit next week.
jess_dev: packages removed from public registry. Need to republish scrubbed package.json. Who will coordinate republish and ensure pre-publish linting?
alex: I'll coordinate republish with infra. Also adding a pre-publish lint to block obvious credentials/SA references.
mike_ops: Postmortem owners assigned: mika_sec (security), alex (dev owner), jess_dev (CI), sam_oncall (ops).
mika_sec: tagging evidence and compliance: copying artifacts to s3://compliance-evidence/incidents/INC-2026-045/ and starting retention hold.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=containment, assignees=[mika_sec,alex,jess_dev,sam_oncall].
sam_oncall: Confirmed the key is disabled and removed from active keys: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=service-account-llm-deploy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` shows 0 active keys.
alex: found two build artifacts referencing that SA in their metadata; rotating and republishing now. ETA ~90m.
sara: please preserve logs for 90 days and export to Splunk. mika_sec, can you file the Splunk export ticket?
mika_sec: filing now. Ticket SPL-4721 created and linked in the incident doc.
jess_dev: CI change: adding prepublish hook:
```
if grep -q 'service-account-llm-deploy' package.json; then
  echo 'found SA reference' && exit 1
fi
```
I'll open a PR with the hook and linter rule.
alex: after rotation we'll run a package-registry token leak scan for the last 6 months and update the runbook. Also consider adding a pre-publish scrubbing step in the release pipeline.
sara: good. Keep compliance and legal in the loop if any packages were downloaded externally.
mika_sec: documenting all steps in the incident playbook. Will run a short postmortem in 48 hours. Thanks team.
